title: Pentecostalism
summary: Pentecostalism grew from the American Holiness movement. Speaking in tongues broke out at Charles Parham's Bible school in Topeka, Kansas, in 1901, and in 1906 William Seymour, a Black Holiness preacher, carried the movement to Los Angeles. His Azusa Street mission became the centre of a revival whose visitors spread it across the nation and abroad within a few years. Stressing baptism in the Spirit, tongues and healing, Pentecostal and charismatic Christianity was estimated in 2001 at 535 million adherents worldwide.

uncertainty.note: Dated from the 1906 Azusa Street revival; the Topeka outbreak of 1901 is generally taken as the movement's start.

as_recorded.value: the famous Azusa Street Revival in Los Angeles lit the Pentecostal spark among Latinos and other racial and ethnic groups beginning in 1906.

Seymour's Azusa Street Apostolic Faith Mission became the center of a great revival, in which visitors to the Azusa mission spread the movement across the nation and around the world in only a few years.
